Physics. Once you start learning how absurd the universe we live in is, I think it's impossible to get bored. The thing that got me most interested many years ago was learning about the speed of light. This is not really explained until relatively high level classes. The speed of light is not a 'speed limit' as is often taught at lower levels. Its the speed limit only of perception. The thing that's not explained is that time itself can change.

A simple example. Imagine we develop a ship that can accelerate towards the speed of light. In a vacuum we know that each time it thrusts it gains 1000km/s more velocity. The speed of light is a shade under 300,000km/s. So what happens on the 300th thrust? From the perspective of the person in the ship - nothing changes and it can happily continue accelerating away in a basic Newtonian fashion. But.. speed limits!? The crazy thing is what happens to a person watching the ship. As the ship's velocity increases, from the perspective of an observer it's kinetic energy increases. As shown by the famous equation e=mc2, energy and mass are proportional. That means as its velocity increases and thus its energy increases, its mass increases. Consequently each thrust gives less and less velocity to the ship from this observer's perspective. And the amount of energy needed to accelerate the ship as the ship's velocity approaches the speed of light, approaches infinity.

So... how does all of this work out in reality? When the ship slows down, comes back home and the pilot meets the observer? Time itself changes. The passage of time for the person in the ship will slow down relative to the person back on the planet observing him. Every second for the person in the ship might be an hour, a day or even longer relative to the person back on the planet. So our pilot may travel half a light year out, turn back around and come home. Given our insane acceleration capacity in this ship this trip might have just taken him a a few minutes or hours. But when he gets back home and lands on the planet, one entire year will have passed for everybody on the planet. They will have seen the ship reach near the speed of light and then travel for a year before coming back.

This isn't a 'trick' or anything like that. Time itself actually changes. This isn't just theoretic. It's been tested numerous times as it's completely mind bogglingly unbelievable. It also has to be compensated for most of all high energy/velocity scientific projects. It also needs to be compensated for in things like GPS satellites. If relativity was not accounted for in GPS satellites, errors would accumulate to the tune of 10km per day! Think about how ridiculous it is that time travel (forward only) is actually a genuine part of our reality.

I've left some things out to simplify the model (in particular space/distance itself also dilates alongside time) but everything that's stated here is completely accurate. If this interests you some of the key words for googling and further information would be things like: time dilation, length contraction, twin paradox, relativity, and mass-energy equivalence.
